hint.title: Match coefficients
hint.text: If \((x+k)\) is a factor, the expression is \((x+k)(\dots)\). Expand and match the x-coefficient to each choice; keep the one where k is a positive integer.

hint.title: SOH, then Pythagoras
hint.text: Use \(\sin=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}\) to find one leg. Then \(a^2+b^2=c^2\) for the other leg.

hint.title: Touches once
hint.text: A horizontal line meets a parabola exactly once only at the vertex. Complete the square to get vertex form; you want the vertex's y-value.
Legs \(x, x\), hypotenuse \(x\sqrt2\). Perimeter \(=2x+x\sqrt2\). Solve for \(x\), then multiply by \(\sqrt2\).

hint.title: Discriminant = 0
hint.text: Subtract one equation from the other to get a single quadratic \(=0\). Exactly one solution → \(b^2-4ac=0\).

hint.title: Root → exponent
hint.text: Rewrite the root as a fraction exponent: \(\sqrt[n]{x^m}=x^{m/n}\). Combine with exponent rules (multiply → add, divide → subtract) and match exponents.

hint.title: No solution
hint.text: No solution = parallel lines: same slope, different y-intercept. Put each choice in \(y=mx+b\) form and compare with the given line.

hint.title: Decay model
hint.text: Loses r% → multiply by \(1-r\). 'Every N minutes' → the exponent is \(\dfrac tN\).

hint.title: Sample bias
hint.text: Who was surveyed, and where? Would families at a playground have more children than a typical household?

hint.title: No solution
hint.text: Line both up as \(Ax+By=C\). Whatever multiplies one x-coefficient to get the other must also multiply the y-coefficient.

hint.title: Tangent ⊥ radius
hint.text: Slope of the radius (center → touching point), then flip and negate for the tangent. Which point makes that slope with the touching point?

hint.title: One equation
hint.text: Get all the x's on one side so it looks like \(ax+b=cx+d\). Different x-coefficients → one solution. Same → compare the constants.

hint.title: SOH
hint.text: \(\sin=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}\). From the marked angle: which side is across from it, and which side is the longest?

hint.title: Absolute value
hint.text: Get the absolute value alone first. Then split: \(u=k\) or \(u=-k\). Solve both and add.

hint.title: Center + radius
hint.text: Read the center from the equation (signs flip). The radius is the distance from the center to one end of the diameter.

hint.title: What does it mean?
hint.text: An x-intercept is where the output is 0. Here the output is height. What is happening when the height is 0?

hint.title: Volume
hint.text: \(V=\pi r^2h\). Plug each choice's radius and height in and compare. Doubling r multiplies V by 4.

hint.title: Totals
hint.text: Sum = mean × count. Write the full total with the missing value as a letter. The full mean is a whole number, so the total must divide evenly.

hint.title: Similar triangles
hint.text: A segment parallel to one side cuts off a smaller similar triangle. Set up \(\dfrac{\text{big}}{\text{small}}=\dfrac{\text{big}}{\text{small}}\) with matching sides.

hint.title: Factor
hint.text: Write the expression as (given factor) × (another factor), expand, and match coefficients. Or spot a difference of squares: \(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)\).

hint.title: Growth factor
hint.text: Rewrite so the exponent counts the step the question uses (\(\frac{x}{\text{step}}\)). The new base is the multiplier; turn it into a percent (e.g. \(1.2\to20\%\)).

hint.title: Same base
hint.text: Plug \(x+2\) into f. Then split the exponent with \(a^{m+n}=a^m\cdot a^n\) and multiply the plain numbers together.

hint.title: Totals
hint.text: Total = mean × count. The median is the middle value (find its position). Range = biggest − smallest. You get two equations—add them.

hint.title: Find the combo
hint.text: Don't solve for x and y separately. Add the two equations and look at what appears. Then scale it to what the question asks for.

hint.title: Probability
hint.text: Probability = what you want ÷ total. Count the numbers in the set, then the ones that are even AND at or below the limit.

hint.title: Circle equation
hint.text: Complete the square to find the center and \(r\). Double the radius, then write \((x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2\)—square the new radius.

hint.title: new = old × (1 ± r)
hint.text: 'p% greater than' → multiply by \(1+\frac p{100}\). 'p% less than' → multiply by \(1-\frac p{100}\). Find the second number first.

hint.title: Given that
hint.text: 'Given that it's tall' → your total is only the tall trees. Tall maples ÷ all tall trees.

hint.title: Compare the slopes
hint.text: Exactly one solution → the lines cross → different slopes. For \(Ax+By=C\) the slope is \(-\dfrac AB\). Which choice has a different slope?

hint.title: Vertex
hint.text: The minimum is at the vertex. Use the factors: the vertex is halfway between the two zeros. (Or expand and use \(x=-\dfrac{b}{2a}\).)

hint.title: Best-fit slope
hint.text: 'Increase in fat for every 1 gram of protein' = the slope of the line. Pick two points ON the line, compute rise ÷ run.

hint.title: Scale by k
hint.text: Lengths × k → areas × \(k^2\).

hint.title: Translate the words
hint.text: 'is' → =, 'of' → ×, 'p%' → \(\frac p{100}\). Write both sentences as equations, substitute one into the other, then find what percent one is of the other.

hint.title: No solution
hint.text: Write both as \(Ax+By=C\). No solution → \(\dfrac{A_1}{A_2}=\dfrac{B_1}{B_2}\) but the C's don't match. Set the A-ratio equal to the B-ratio and solve.

hint.title: Quadratic formula
hint.text: Move everything to one side: \(ax^2+bx+c=0\). Then \(x=\dfrac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\). Simplify the root and divide through by 2.

hint.title: Similar → same trig
hint.text: Matching angles in similar triangles have the same tan. Use \(\tan=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}\) in the second triangle.

hint.title: Read the graph
hint.text: Distance walked during that time = (y at the end) − (y at the start). Read both y-values off the line.

hint.title: Angles
hint.text: Parallel lines make matching angles equal, so there's another right angle. Then use 'triangle = 180' and 'straight line = 180'.

hint.title: Slice of a circle
hint.text: \(\dfrac{\text{angle}}{360^\circ}=\dfrac{\text{arc length}}{\text{circumference}}\). Solve for the circumference.

hint.title: Match coefficients
hint.text: Expand the given form and match the \(x^2\), x, and number parts to the expression. Any one match gives the constant.

hint.title: Compare the numbers
hint.text: 'At least one solution' = same line OR crossing lines. Only parallel lines (same slope, different intercept) fail. Is each equation a multiple of the given one, or a different slope?

hint.title: Vertex
hint.text: Minimum = vertex. Find the two zeros from the factors and take their midpoint, or complete the square.

hint.title: Angles
hint.text: Two equal sides → two equal base angles. Triangle sum = 180 gives them; then straight line = 180 for the outside angle.

hint.title: Perpendicular slopes
hint.text: Rewrite line k as \(y=mx+b\) to see its slope. Perpendicular → flip and negate it. Then use the given y-intercept as \(b\).

hint.title: y-intercept
hint.text: The y-intercept is the value when \(x=0\). Which year does \(x=0\) stand for here?

hint.title: Similar → same tan
hint.text: The figure has three similar right triangles, so matching angles have the same tangent. Use \(\tan=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}\) where you know a side.

hint.title: Discriminant = 0
hint.text: Solve the line for y, plug into the parabola, move everything to one side. Exactly one point → \(b^2-4ac=0\). Keep the positive value.
Sides are \(x,\ x\sqrt3,\ 2x\). Add them, set equal to the perimeter, solve for \(x\). The longest side is \(2x\).

hint.title: Random sample
hint.text: You can only generalize to the group the sample was randomly drawn from. Which students was it drawn from?

hint.title: Vertex is halfway
hint.text: The vertex's x-value is exactly halfway between the x-intercepts: \(h=\dfrac{p+q}{2}\). Plug in the vertex x and the known intercept, solve for the other.

hint.title: Translate the words
hint.text: 'A is p% of B' → \(A=\frac p{100}B\). Write both sentences this way, solve the first, plug into the second.

hint.title: Tangent ⊥ radius
hint.text: Find the slope of the radius from the center to the touching point, then flip and negate it.

hint.title: Zero → factor
hint.text: Find the x-values in the table where \(p(x)=0\). Each gives a factor \((x-k)\)—watch the sign flip.

hint.title: Discriminant = 0
hint.text: Substitute the first equation into the second to get one quadratic \(=0\). Exactly one solution → \(b^2-4ac=0\). Solve for the constant.

hint.title: Slice of a circle
hint.text: Arcs are in the same ratio as their central angles. Find the angle for the arc you want (angles around the center add to 360°).

hint.title: Exterior angle
hint.text: The lines form a triangle. Exterior angle = sum of the two far inside angles. Use 'straight line = 180' for any missing inside angle.

hint.title: Factor by grouping
hint.text: Expand, then factor by grouping into two factors. Set each to 0, then multiply the two solutions. (Shortcut: product \(=\dfrac ca\).)

hint.title: Complete the square
hint.text: Complete the square on x and on y. The number left on the right side is \(r^2\). Set it equal to (given radius)\(^2\) and solve.

hint.title: Read the exponent
hint.text: The base \(b\) is applied each time the exponent goes up by 1. How many years make the exponent go up by 1? Convert that to months.

hint.title: Slice of a circle
hint.text: \(\dfrac{\text{angle}}{360^\circ}=\dfrac{\text{arc}}{2\pi r}\). Plug in the arc's angle and length, solve for r.

hint.title: Root → exponent
hint.text: Write every root as a fraction exponent. Multiply the plain numbers; add the exponents of the same base. Match to the given form.

hint.title: Similar triangles
hint.text: The altitude makes smaller right triangles that are similar. Match corresponding sides and set big/small = big/small.

hint.title: Plug it in
hint.text: Plug each x-value into the inequality to find the cutoff for y. Then find the table where all three y-values land on the correct side.

hint.title: Discriminant < 0
hint.text: Substitute to get one quadratic. No real solutions → \(b^2-4ac<0\). Solve the inequality, then take the smallest integer that works.

hint.title: Shift
hint.text: Up k units → \(g(x)=f(x)+k\). Plug the x-value into f first, then add.
Use the coordinates to get each triangle's leg lengths. Equal legs + a right angle → the other two angles are 45°. Write that in the units the choices use.

hint.title: Absolute value
hint.text: Get the absolute value by itself. Can an absolute value ever equal a negative number?

hint.title: Median vs. mean
hint.text: Find the middle position before and after adding the new value. A value bigger than the mean pulls the mean up—does the middle value change?

hint.title: Percent change
hint.text: Decreasing by p% means multiplying by \(1-\frac{p}{100}\). Simplify the expression to (number) × quantity and set that number equal to \(1-\frac p{100}\).

hint.title: TOA, then Pythagoras
hint.text: \(\tan=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}\) gives the missing leg. Then \(a^2+b^2=c^2\) for the hypotenuse. Perimeter = all three sides added.

hint.title: Random sample
hint.text: Results apply to the group the sample was randomly picked from—no bigger. What exactly were the trees picked from?

hint.title: y = a·bᵗ
hint.text: Percent more each year → \(b=1+r\). Then use the given count in the given year to find the start value \(a\). Careful: t counts years after the start year.

hint.title: Circle equation
hint.text: Get circle A into \((x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2\). Moving right changes only \(h\); the radius stays the same.

hint.title: Median
hint.text: Put the 7 percents in order and take the 4th. Then subtract.

hint.title: Radius + right angle
hint.text: Both segments from the center are radii (equal). Find the radius with the distance formula. A right angle between two radii → hypotenuse \(=r\sqrt2\).

hint.title: Slope
hint.text: Read two clean points off the line: \(m=\dfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}\). The point with the unknown is on the same line, so it gives the same slope. Set them equal and solve.

hint.title: Undo the square
hint.text: \(u^2=k\) means \(u=\sqrt k\) or \(u=-\sqrt k\). Solve both, then add. (Shortcut: sum \(=-\dfrac ba\).)

hint.title: Spread
hint.text: Symmetric plots: the median is the middle value. For SD, which plot has more dots far from the center?

hint.title: sin/cos swap
hint.text: For acute angles, \(\sin A=\cos B\) means \(A+B=90\). Add the two expressions, set equal to 90, solve.

hint.title: Vertex form + symmetry
hint.text: Use \(y=a(x-h)^2+k\) with the maximum as the vertex. A parabola is symmetric: the launch height comes back the same distance past the vertex.
